articles.title: NFL: Aaron Donald comes out of retirement to rejoin Los Angeles Rams
articles.summary: Aaron Donald, one of the NFL's greatest defensive players, has come out of retirement to rejoin his former side Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald, one of the NFL's greatest defensive players, has come out of retirement to rejoin his former side Los Angeles Rams.

The 35-year-old announced his immediate retirement in March 2024 after spending 10 seasons in the NFL, all with the Rams.

Donald, who was the 13th overall pick by the Rams in the 2014 draft, will rejoin on a reported one-year deal worth $20m. , external

"We back," he posted on social media, with a video of his career highlights.

He helped the Rams win the Super Bowl in 2022 and is one of three men to be named the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year three times.

Donald finished his career with 117 sacks, two of them coming in the Rams' Super Bowl win.

He became the fastest defensive tackle to reach 100 sacks in NFL history and was an eight-time All-Pro selection.

articles.title: How Aaron Donald's NFL Comeback Impacts Rams' Super Bowl Odds, Comeback Player of the Year Race
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are now the prohibitive betting favorites to win the Super Bowl after Aaron Donald came out of retirement and rejoined the team on Sunday, pairing with Myles Garrett to give them a frightening defensive line.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are now the prohibitive betting favorites to win the Super Bowl after Aaron Donald came out of retirement and rejoined the team on Sunday, pairing with Myles Garrett to give them a frightening defensive line.

Following the Rams in the Super Bowl odds are the Buffalo Bills (+1000), the defending-champion Seattle Seahawks (+1100), the Baltimore Ravens (+1300) and four teams at +1700 (Detroit Lions, Los Angeles Chargers, Kansas City Chiefs, Houston Texans), per FanDuel .

The Rams have had quite the offseason, adding Garrett, Donald, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Not bad for a team that reached the NFC Championship Game last season, losing a thriller to the Seahawks. The betting public clearly is very high on L.A. heading into the 2026 season.

And Donald will be a popular pick to Comeback Player of the Year, though questions remain how he will hold up after two seasons away from the sport.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. making the Giants is one of the coolest stories of the NFL season
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. was a star during his first stint with the Giants.
articles.body:
When Odell Beckham Jr. was asked during the New York Giants' last preseason game what it would mean to make the roster, he had a heartfelt response.

"It would mean everything," Beckham said during the Giants' broadcast . "It would be my dream. This is where I started. There's no place I want to give my whole heart to, more than anything else in the world, is this place right here."

Giants fans might have expressed the exact same sentiment.

Beckham and the Giants have officially come full circle. Beckham made the 53-man roster , according to reports, giving the 33-year-old Beckham a chance to finish his career where it started. Beckham might not have a huge impact on the offense, especially not like he did his first few seasons with the team, but it's a great story to have one of the most charismatic athletes of the past 15 years back in New York.

When Beckham signed a one-year deal worth the veteran minimum of $1.3 million on June 1, it was a novel footnote of a faded star trying to have another tour with his first team. But after being out of football in 2025, following unsuccessful seasons with the Ravens and Dolphins the two years before, Beckham showed enough to make the team.

Beckham had an up-and-down preseason. He made seven catches for 76 yards, and it would have been even better if Jameis Winston hadn't overthrown him after a great move to get wide open deep downfield in the preseason finale. But he also also dropped a pass in the end zone in the Giants' second preseason game and in the finale he had a pass go off his hands for an interception.

Nevertheless, Giants coach John Harbaugh endorsed Beckham after the preseason finale.

"He has done enough to make an NFL roster, for sure," Harbaugh said after the preseason finale. "He's played well. He's gotten better as camp's gone along. He deserves credit for that. He's done a really good job with it."

Like Allen Iverson going back to play with the Philadelphia 76ers, Randy Moss spending a few games with the Minnesota Vikings years after he was traded, Rickey Henderson going back to the Oakland A's at age 39 or Dwyane Wade finishing up his career with the Miami Heat, the nostalgia of Beckham being back on the Giants is off the charts.

Beckham was a first-round pick and NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year with the Giants in 2014. He became one of the biggest stars in sports, and will forever be known for a one-handed catch he made at MetLife Stadium, considered one of the greatest plays in NFL history.

In 2019 Beckham was traded to the Cleveland Browns and never quite recaptured the form he had during his Giants career. He was a key part of the Los Angeles Rams' 2021 championship team, catching the first touchdown of Super Bowl LVI. He also tore an ACL in that Super Bowl, and didn't play at all the next season. He hasn't been much of a factor since that injury.

Maybe Beckham's entire career would have turned out differently if he never was traded from the Giants. There's no way to know. But Giants fans get another chance to cheer him before he exits the NFL. There won't be many better stories than that this season.

articles.title: Winners and Losers from Every NFL Team's 2026 Roster Cuts
articles.summary: And then there were 1,696.
articles.body:
That's how many players are left on NFL rosters after Sunday's 6:00 PM deadline to cut down to 53 active players. For some, it's the realization of a lifelong dream. For others, it's a devastating disappointment—although some of the sting may get taken out when they are scooped up by another team or land on a practice squad.

It's essentially the final step before teams gather to begin preparing in earnest for Week 1. The final domino falling before the regular season begins.

It's also the day that megastar defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of retirement to join the Rams again—because Los Angeles wasn't terrifying enough yet.

Cutdown day all but puts a bow on the offseason. So, as we start the countdown to the rematch of Super Bowl LX that will kick off the 2026 season, let's look at some winners and losers for all 32 teams—from Sunday and before.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

Seventh-round picks have their work cut out for them to even make the 53-man roster, let alone make an impact as a rookie. But Williams fared so well in camp that he has moved all the way up to the second unit, seeing snaps at both tackle spots.

A 6'4", 307-pounder, Williams was a 15-game starter at right tackle for an Ole Miss team that made the College Football Playoff last year. He also has experience playing on the left side, making 19 starts from 2022 to 2024 for the Rebels.

It was no secret that Trey Benson was on the roster bubble after the Cardinals signed Tyler Allgeier and drafted Jeremiyah Love, and sure enough the former third-round pick was waived with an injury designation before clearing waivers and landing back in the desert on injured reserve.

That's the theme with Benson—he just hasn't been able to stay on the field. After James Conner got hurt last year Benson got his chance to show the Redbirds what he could do, only to suffer a knee injury after just one game—an injury that flared back up this summer and prevented Benson from practicing.

When the Falcons used a fourth-round pick on Daniels, they were drafting traits and athleticism. But as Marc Raimondi wrote for ESPN , after an impressive summer there's a real chance that the 6'5" 242-pounder opens the season as one of the starters at inside linebacker.

"The Falcons have trusted him with the green dot at times this summer because of injuries," he said, "and Daniels has a legitimate shot at starting at inside linebacker alongside Divine Deablo."

With Michael Penix Jr. sidelined or limited throughout most of camp and the preseason, the starting quarterback job in Atlanta (at least early in the season) was Tagovailoa's to lose.

Well, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL.com , Tagovailoa has done his level best to lose it.

"It really seemed that the goal of the entire organization was to have Tua be the starting quarterback right away to start the season," Rapoport said. "Let Michael Penix come along slow. Tua's play made that impossible, not just in the preseason game, which we've seen, but it sounds like practice as well. All of which is to say, this is Michael Penix's job for the taking."

There's little doubt who the star of the summer in Baltimore has been—third-round wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane has seemingly received rave reviews from the first time he stepped on the practice field, and those accolades have continued pouring in as we moved into training camp and then the preseason.

Lane has already all but sewn up the No. 3 wide receiver role for the Ravens, and it wouldn't be a huge shock if he overtakes Rashod Bateman as the team's No. 2 wideout at some point this season.

In recent years, the Ravens have spent a lot of draft capital on the edge-rusher position. That the team tried to trade for Maxx Crosby before signing Trey Hendrickson essentially tells you how that has worked out.

Back in 2024, the Ravens used a third-round pick on Isaac, but he has barely seen the field since, He spent most of the 2024 season on the NFL list, missed all of the 2025 season with an elbow injury and was sidelined most of the summer.

They say the best ability is availability—and given that Isaac hasn't been, it's not that surprising to see him on the outside of the edge-rusher rotation looking in.

The Buffalo Bills are one of the leading candidates to represent the AFC in Super Bowl LXI. But to get to SoFi Stadium, the team needs to be more consistent rushing the passer after logging just 36 sacks last year.

We have yet to see a game that counts, but the Bills appear to be improved in that regard entering 2026.

Veteran free agent addition Bradley Chubb is healthy and has looked good on the practice field. So has rookie T.J. Parker, who also had a solid preseason. With Gregory Rousseau also in the mix, the Bills have the makings of a promising three-man rotation.

There was a time when Mecole Hardman was regarded as a rising young talent at wide receiver—he was a Pro Bowler as a rookie and won three Super Bowls with the Kansas City Chiefs.

But since a 59/693/2 line with the Chiefs in 2021, Hardman's production fell off a cliff—he hasn't had even 300 receiving yards in a season since, he was targeted just 14 times in his second stint with the Chiefs last year and after a drop-filled preseason Hardman isn't resurrecting his career in Western New York.

Jonathon Brooks was the first running back selected in the 2024 draft after a standout career at Texas, but his NFL career has been non-existent to date—he started it on the bench rehabbing an ACL tear suffered at Texas, finally got his chance to play and carried the ball all of nine times before tearing that same ACL again.

Now, after missing the entire 2025 season, Brooks is healthy again. His numbers in the preseason weren't especially impressive, but with veteran back Chuba Hubbard nursing a hamstring injury there's a real chance that when the Panthers face the Chicago Bears in Week 1 that Brooks will be the Panthers' lead back.

Over his first two seasons with the Panthers, Wallace made 20 starts, so entering the summer the prevailing wisdom was that it would be Wallace starting alongside Devin Lloyd at inside linebacker for the Panthers.

However, the struggles defending the run that plagued Wallace over his first two seasons have been evident on the practice field and in the preseason, and despite just six starts over three years it's Claudin Cherelus who appears in line to open the 2026 campaign as Lloyd's running mate in the middle of the Carolina defense.

Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson has seen his workload decrease in all three of his professional seasons—from 81 carries as a rookie to 55 carries in 2024 to all of to totes in seven games.

With Salvon Ahmed showing out in the preseason, there was more than a little speculation that Johnson's roster spot could be in jeopardy. But "The Turk" came for Ahmed instead, and Johnson will be back for a fourth season in the Windy City.

And with Kyle Monangai banged up, it will likely be Johnson who starts the season as D'Andre Swift's primary backup in Chicago.

It might seem a little odd to call a player who will likely be the Week 1 starter at left tackle a "loser," but the only thing that might be more accurate would be labeling Bears quarterback Caleb Williams one.

Because the last thing Williams should want is Jones protecting his blind side against Jaelan Phillips and the Carolina Panthers.

It has been a rough summer for the fifth-year veteran—including ab abysmal preseason outing against the Bengals where Jones was manhandled by Cincinnati's backups.

Ozzy Trapilo can't get healthy soon enough.

Much has been made of the additions of veteran Boye Mafe and rookie Cashius Howell on the defensive line. But as Paul Dehner wrote for The Athletic , third-year pro Cedric Johnson has been building on a quietly solid 2025 season.

"He's popped multiple times, bending around the edge nearly untouched, and earned a few reps against the first team as the defense rotates," he said. "Johnson's built more like Mafe and less like the smaller Howell, but the 2024 sixth-round pick looks to be blossoming. Johnson produced a pressure once every 7.9 pass-rush snaps last season. That ranked second among Bengals edge rushers, narrowly topped by Trey Hendrickson at 7.7."

Johnson had 20 tackles and two sacks in just 207 snaps last year, and if the summer is any indication he's looking to build on that in 2026.

The Bengals took a buzzsaw to their leaky defense in both free agency and the NFL Draft. The offense is loaded with skill-position talent. But there's one unit that has long been an issue in the Queen City—and it still is.

The Bengals spent a big chunk of the 2025 with an offensive line that ranked at the bottom of the NFL , and that line is essentially unchanged this year.

It looks it—Joe Burrow made it all of two dropbacks into the preseason before getting sacked.

The Browns are barreling toward a very Cleveland season. The quarterback competition that dominated summer headlines is over—the Browns are rolling out Deshaun Watson and his al dente arm in Week 1 despite the fact the team's fans actively loathe him.

The revamped offensive line has been inconsistent. The skill-position players are mostly very young. The defense will be decent, but with Myles Garrett gone it won't be as stout as it was in 2025—and depth in the secondary is a major issue.

The Browns may not be the worst team in the NFL. But they are on the short list for that "honor."

A third-round pick of the Browns back in 2023, Cedric Tillman had a flash or two over three seasons in Cleveland—over a three-game span in 2024, he caught 21 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns.

But durability has been a constant issue with Tillman—he's missed at least three games in all three seasons, including four in a 2025 season in which Tillman caught just 21 passes.

With rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston standing out in camp, Tillman became expendable in Cleveland—and the Browns released him earlier in the week.

When the Cowboys drafted Barham in the third round in April, it was a pick that appeared more about depth and the future—with DeMarvion Overshown and Dee Winters seemingly locked in as the starters, Barham was a developmental piece for a revamped Dallas defense.

Unless he's already developed, of course.

Barham has consistently impressed over the summer, including five tackles and a tackle for loss in his preseason debut in just 18 snaps. Barham may not have bumped Winters from the starting lineup just yet—but the clock could be ticking.

It wouldn't be cutdown day without a surprise or two. One came on Sunday in Dallas.

Mind you, it's not like Jaydon Blue tore it up as a rookie—the fifth-rounder averaged just 3.4 yards per carry last year as Javonte Williams' backup with the Cowboys. But given what the Cowboys did (or didn't do) at running back in the offseason, the general belief was that Blue would be back for a second season as Williams' understudy.

The Cowboys apparently didn't share that assessment—and given the team's (now) lack of depth at running back, it's a safe bet that Dalls will be scooping up someone who got shown the door just like Blue did.

Bo Nix had a fantastic second NFL season, leading the Broncos to the AFC's best record. But that season ended in disastrous fashion—Nix broke his ankle in the Divisional Round. That ankle has been one of the dominant storylines in the Mile High City.

Nix has been the subject of positive reports throughout the summer, and he was in midseason form in limited preseason action.

The Broncos added a weapon for Nix in the offseason in Jaylen Waddle and bolstered the ground game with bruising rookie Jonah Coleman.

With Nik looking 100 percent, this defense could be dangerous.

No team in the NFL had more success rushing the passer last year than the Broncos, who paced the league with 68 sacks.

That pass rush was dealt a blow on Sunday.

Veteran edge-rusher Jonathon Cooper, who was second on the team with eight sacks, was placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List after a pair of arrests in June.

It shouldn't have come as a surprise to the team, and the Broncos still have edge-rusher Nik Bonitto and defensive tackle Zach Allen up front. But it's the second starter from last year's defensive line the Broncos have lost this offseason.

A fifth-round rookie out of Arizona State, Abney has so impressed in camp that he started in the slot in Detroit's second preseason game. He told reporters that he's trying to take full advantage of those first-team reps.

"I'm just coming out here trying to learn every day and take advantage of those reps that I'm getting (with the first team)" Abney said. "Just doing my assignment, executing that, not trying to do too much. Just trying to be consistent and earn the trust of my coaches and teammates so I can continue getting these reps."

Whether Abney starts the season opener is yet to be determined. But the youngster locked down a spot on the 53-man roster.

Back in 2021, Wilson made four starts for the Dallas Cowboys and caught 45 passes for 602 yards and six touchdowns. But by this point in his career, the 30-year-old was just hoping to earn a spot at the back of the bench for the Lions at wide receiver.

Wilson didn't make many waves in camp and played sparingly in the preseason, and after he got hurt in an exhibition game against the Washington Commanders the Lions placed Wilson on injured reserve before waiving him with an injury settlement.

For much of the offseason, it appeared that this was the end of the line for veteran tight end Jonnu Smith—after barely cracking 200 receiving yards and averaging just 5.8 yards per catch with the Pittsburgh Steelers last year, the 31-year-old languished most of the summer without a team.

But with Luke Musgrave looking likely to open the 2026 season on the PUP list with a neck injury, the Packers needed depth at the position—especially with Tucker Kraft working his way back from an ACL tear.

Not only does Smith have a new team, but he could see the field quite a bit early in the season.

It has been a rocky offseason for Josh Jacobs, who was arrested and later charged with a pair of misdemeanors after a domestic incident in May--an incident severe enough that the NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List Sunday.

With Jacobs now out indefinitely, the Packers traded for Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson, who will join a backfield that includes Marshawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks.

Brooks has played sparingly to date. Lloyd has struggled to stay healthy--six carries for 15 yards in two seasons. Johnson was a major disappointment in Pittsburgh.

The news isn't totally unexpected, but it blew a sizable hole in the offense of a team with playoff aspirations.

Boutte showed some promise in New England last year, hauling in 33 passes for 551 yards and six scores. But with A.J. Brown now in New England, Boutte's role with the Patriots was cloudy—so much so that Pats head coach Mike Vrabel said that Boutte would likely have been a healthy scratch as often as not this year.

Of course, Vrabel said that after Boutte was dealt to the Texans—where he will most assuredly not be inactive on game days. In fact, with Jayden Higgins out for the year with an ACL tear, Boutte will likely open the season as Houston's starting "Z" receiver opposite Nico Collins.

Just a few days before the Boutte trade, the Texans signed Shepard off the street to help compensate for the Higgins injury. But now Shepard is behind Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson Boutte on the depth chart.

That's far too many names for a player who just got to town to move past before final cuts—even a player who has spent 10 years catching passes at the professional level.

This is probably it for Shepard's NFL career.

There's no question that Jonathan Taylor is the lead running back for the Indianapolis Colts. But after leading the NFL in carries last year, the Colts would be well-advised to find a way to lighten the load on their bellcow back.

The team may have found one—in a seventh-round rookie.

After tallying 725 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns last year at Kentucky, McGowan appears to have locked down the role of the team's No. 2 back, drawing praise from head coach Shane Steichen.

"He's running hard, he's seeing it good," Steichen told reporters . "And I've said it before, but the physicality that he runs with, we want that and he brings that to our roster. We're really excited about that."

Back in March, the Colts acquired veteran defensive tackle Colby Wooden in a trade for linebacker Zaire Franklin. A 6'4", 273-pounder who amassed 50 tackles in Green Bay a year ago, Wooden had a quiet preseason. But on the heels of a decent showing in training camp, the fourth-year pro's roster spot was believed to be relatively safe.

While many pundits expected that former first-round pick Jerry Tillery would be the odd man out at defensive tackle, it was Wooden who was let go as part of the final cuts.

It would be a little ironic if he winds up back with the Packers—meaning that the Colts essentially gave Franklin to Green Bay for free.

In Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers, the Jaguars possess one of the best three-deep depth charts in the league at wide receiver.

But if training camp and the preseason are any indication, there's no question who the No. 1 wideout in Jacksonville is.

Whether it was in joint practices or in limited preseason action, Trevor Lawrence repeatedly looked to Washington as his primary red—and far more often than not the fourth-year pro responded.

Now the Jaguars just need to open the ol' checkbook and pay the man.

The tale of J'Mari Taylor is a reminder that it's a long way from OTAs to the final roster cutdown. An undrafted rookie out of Virginia, Taylor was one of the stars of early workouts, with pundits talking up his vision, patience and ability to catch the ball out of the backfield.

Then the pads went on, and the shine came off.

Taylor wasn't able to carry over his positive momentum into training camp, and while there were a couple of flashes Taylor is the clear No. 4 back (at best) behind Bhayshul Tuten, Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah.

Fourth running backs wind up on practice squads.

To be clear, despite the rave reviews that Allen has earned throughout the offseason and the stats he put up during the preseason, the fifth-round pick out of Cincinnati isn't going to play a big role offensively early in his rookie season. The Chiefs appear set with their top-three wide receivers in Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Tyquan Thornton.

But Allen was a Day 3 pick who entered the NFL with exactly zero hype. That the youngster fared so well over the summer that he has been viewed as a lock to make the 53-man roster for some time now is an achievement in and of itself.

Not that long ago, it appeared that the Chiefs had found a diamond in the rough in offensive tackle Esa Pole, who went from an undrafted free agent to making five starts for the team after Josh Simmons got hurt.

But Pole's NFL dream has rapidly become a nightmare. A lineman who was once expected to potentially be Kansas City's Week 1 swing tackle simply vanished from the conversation. There was no buzz in camp. When Pole played in the preseason it was with the scrubs--and even then he didn't fare especially well.

On Sunday the Chiefs threw in the towel and released him.

The Las Vegas Raiders got quite the scare recently when Ashton Jeanty went down with an ankle injury. The team appears to have dodged the proverbial bullet with the star running back, but Jeanty's Week 1 availability is very much in jeopardy.

That injury makes Mike Washington's standout camp and preseason all the more important for the silver and black.

A fourth-round pick in April's draft out of Arkansas, Washington shined throughout the summer, including eight carries for 49 yards in the preseason finale against the 49ers.

If Jeanty can't go against the Dolphins in Week 1, Washington will get a chance to show he can do the same in a game that counts.

OK, before we go any farther, let's just everyone take a breath. Rookie quarterbacks struggling isn't new in the NFL. Just ask Peyton Manning. And Troy Aikman.

Fernando Mendoza may well turn out to be a quality NFL starter in his own right. But Mendoza's choppy preseason is a reminder that making the jump from college to the pros is not easy. And that Mendoza has a lot to learn about working his reads and managing pressure in the pocket after playing in a one-read, RPO-heavy scheme at Indiana.

Based on what we saw from Mendoza, it could be a while before we see him in a regular-season game.

Thompson showed off his wheels at this year's scouting combine, peeling off a 4.26-second 40-yard dash. But at just 5'9" and 164 pounds, Thompson's lack of size relegated him to Day 3 pick status.

Well, sometimes big things come in small packages—and after an impressive offseason, Thompson has gone from fighting for a roster spot to potentially seeing meaningful playing time, although he told reporters that there's still plenty of work to do.

"I'm nowhere near where I want to be right now," Thompson said. "I think if I was, there would be issues."

The offensive line for the Chargers was an injury-marred mess in 2025. The team has Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back at tackle, but along the interior history may unfortunately be repeating itself.

The loss of center Tyler Biadasz to a season-ending knee injury was one of the biggest hits any team in the league took over the past month. Rookie Jake Slaughter will slot as the new center, but he had been working at left guard, so the Bolts will also have to pivot to Kayode Awosika at that spot.

The inside of the offensive line in L.A. is shaky—and the season hasn't even started yet.

When the Rams made Ty Simpson a top-15 pick in April's draft, more than a few eyebrows went skyward—it was a pick for the future made by a team that is most assuredly in "win-now" mode.

As it turns out, Les Snead just might know what he's doing.

Simpson was easily the best rookie quarterback of the preseason, even if much of the damage was done against backups--Simpson finished the preseason with a 78.3 completion percentage, going 47-for-60 with 382 passing yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions.

There aren't a lot of open roster spots available on a roster as loaded with talent as the Rams. But linebacker is one of the weaker position groups on the team, and given Monty Rice's five years of NFL experience, 11 career starts (including six with the Tennessee Titans in 2022) and special teams experience, Rice likely signed with the Rams in the hopes he could chase a ring playing kick and punt coverage.

The 27-year-old will have to try to latch on elsewhere though—Rice was among the first wave of cuts the Super Bowl favorites made on Saturday.

It might seem a bit strange to call a guy who barely practiced until recently a "winner," but for Chris Bell, getting in Miami's preseason finale after tearing his ACL at Louisville last November was a win.

Bell posted modest stats in the game (two catches, 22 yards), but Bell told reporters that it was great to be back out there and he'll be ready for the opener against the Raiders.

"I'll be ready. I'm ready now, but I definitely will be ready in two weeks. I really needed this game, just to step out on the NFL field and play against some competition, other than my teammates in practice. So, I 100 percent will be ready," Bell said.

Last year, veteran linebacker Tyrel Dodson wore the "green dot" helmet communicator and made a career-high 129 total tackles for the Dolphins.

When the Dolphins drafted Jacob Rodriguez in the second round of April's draft, the writing was on the wall that Dodson's days as a starter were numbered. But it was still jarring to see the seventh-year veteran released outright on Sunday.

When the Minnesota Vikings used a first-round pick on Banks back in April, they had to know it was a long-term project—that it would take some time for Banks to get back up to speed as he worked his way back from a foot injury.

Once Banks did get on the practice field that Round 1 talent was evident, and while his preseason action was spent with the second-team Banks showed the power and disruptiveness that got his name called on the 2026 draft's first day.

McCarthy, on the other hand, won't be starting another game for the Vikings. Like, ever.

At this point, there's no sugarcoating it—drafting McCarthy 10th overall in 2024 was a massive mistake. It's not just that McCarthy lost the starting job under center to Kyler Murray. He was also soundly outplayed by Carson Wentz in the competition to back Murray up.

Sitting out the preseason finale with an ankle injury was just the final indignity for the Vikings. McCarthy can't stay on the field, and even when he's out there his play makes you wish he wasn't.

Not that long ago, it appeared that Williams would be hard-pressed to see the field much in 2026. The second-year pro was buried on the depth chart behind A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and Kayshon Boutte.

Now, however, Boutte is catching passes in Houston, and after a three-touchdown preseason Williams has caught the eye of Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel.

"I just want to give Kyle as many opportunities to continue to improve and do the things that we have asked him to improve on," Vrabel told reporters . "I love his ability outside the numbers to be able to stretch the field."

Now all Williams has to do is carry that momentum over into games that count.

The Patriots were an excellent defensive football team last year, and this smacks of nitpicking. But given that the team is already dealing with injuries to the likes of edge-rusher Harold Landry III, the performance of the second-team defense is concerning.

The Pats were shredded in the preseason finals by Dillon Gabriel and a Browns offense that struggled all preseason long to move the ball consistently.

In Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis and Marcus Jones, New England's top-three cornerbacks are set. But behind that things get dicey.

All it would take is one injury to create a potentially glaring weakness on the back end.

Brown arrived in New Orleans a sixth-round pick hoping to just make the team.

He'll enter his rookie season looking to make a real dent in the Saints offense.

Brown was one of the most consistently impressive players in Saints camp, showing excellent route-running skills to go along with elite speed. That speed was on display in the preseason finale, when Brown scored on a reverse.

The Saints will be without Jordyn Tyson until at least October, and after trading Rashid Shaheed the team needs a player who can take the top off defenses and be a threat in the return game.

Jordyn Tyson has the potential to be an outstanding NFL wide receiver. Were it not for one knock, an argument could be made that he was the top receiver in this year's rookie class.

However, that knock keeps knocking—loudly.

The durability issues that plagued Tyson in college carried over to the NFL—he suffered a sever hamstring injury in camp that will land him on the PUP list to begin his NFL career and could keep him out until mid-October—at least.

With Chris Olave also nicked up, the wideout corps in the Big Easy isn't exactly rolling into Week 1.

By most estimations, Deonte Banks first three seasons in the NFL have been a massive disappointment. The 24th overall pick in the 2023 draft has made 35 starts over that span, but his passer rating against was over 120 each of the past two years.

Banks appears to be taking full advantage of a fresh start under new head coach John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson.

Wilson's aggressive scheme calls for a lot of press coverage, and Banks has taken to it well. His offseason wasn't flawless, but the youngster went from potentially being on the roster bubble to having a real shot to start in Week 1.

There's no getting around it—Evan Neal will go down as one of the bigger draft-day boondoggles in Giants' history.

When the Giants selected Neal seventh overall in 2022, he was supposed to be an anchor for the Giants' line for years to come. Neal has been an anchor, all right—around the team's neck.

Neal has just been bad. He was a turnstile at tackle. Things haven't been any better at guard. And after spending most of the summer running with the third-team offense, Neal's status as an all-time bust has been cemented.

Given that the team just drafted Bailey second overall, one would hope that he would be one of the summer's biggest winners on the team. But these sorts of things have been known to go sideways for Gang Green.

Bailey has looked the part of an elite presence on the edge from the moment he stepped onto the practice field, spending more time in the backfield in camp than Breece Hall.

There will still be ups and downs (there always are with rookies at the position), but the Jets got this pick right.

Loser: New York's Other First-Round Picks

The future of the Jets other first-round picks back in April is less certain.

It's far too early to hit the panic button with tight end Kenyon Sadiq—the size, speed and athleticism that got him drafted at No. 16 overall is still there. But Sadiq was something of a "project" already, and all the time he missed over the summer has set his development back.

Wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. had a camp to forget as well—rather than laying claim to the starting job in the slot, Cooper has been on a milk carton, failing to impress in practices or exhibition games.

Cooper is used to scratching and clawing for a roster spot after making the Eagles as an undrafted free agent in 2025. But after making just nine catches on 11 targets in 13 games as a rookie, Cooper entered training camp No. 2 in a familiar position—on the roster bubble.

But Cooper put together a solid training camp, drawing praise from cornerback Tariq Woolen.

"He always goes 100% and whenever you go against him, you know you're going to get a great look," he told reporters . "Coop is a great receiver and to be able to go against him and battle with him and see him grow throughout training camp is a lot of fun."

When Cooper sat out the preseason finale, it was clear that he made the final 53.

Dating back to his time in Kansas City, Steele has long been a fan favorite, whether it's because of his long hair or the reckless abandon he shows with a football in his hands.

Steele was a preseason standout of sorts for the eagles, pacing the team with 14 receptions for 136 yards and two scores. But Steele was far less effective as a runner, averaging just 2.8 yards per carry.

When final cuts came down Sunday, Steele got the axe—although he's a likely practice squad candidate if he clears waivers.

Among Pittsburgh's 2026 rookie class, no one has stood out more than third-year wide receiver Germie Bernard.

Whether it was in minicamp, joint practices or preseason game, the story was the same. Glowing reports. Bernard getting open and making plays. The youngster caught the eyes of many—including franchise legend Ben Roethlisberger.

"Let's talk about Germie Bernard," he said . That's special. That's what I think you're gonna see from him this year, and I think that should excite a lot of people, because of what he has and that potential for the shifty, break a tackle, fast enough, quick enough, get in the end zone. There's gonna be a lot of excitement there."

The former Alabama standout should open his rookie year as the Steelers' third receiver behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr.

The Steelers have dealt with issues along the offensive line for years—issues that Broderick Jones was supposed to help address when the team drafted him in the first round back in 2023.

Instead, as reported by NFL.com , Jones struggled through three seasons of injuries and poor play. Jones has allowed 22 sacks in his career, which is fourth among tackles since 2023, per Pro Football Focus. In 2025, Jones garnered a 57.7 overall PFF grade, which was 70th among 89 qualified offensive tackles.

The Steelers had already passed on Jones' fifth-year option, and earlier this week he was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys.

Sorry, there's no choice here. In 2026, all articles that mention any rookie standouts or winners are legally obligated to mention wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling.

When the 49ers made Stribling the first pick of Round 2, it surprised some. But based on his meteoric rise during the summer, Niners general manager John Lynch appears to have known what he was doing.

It wasn't at all surprising to see Stribling on the sideline for San Francisco's preseason finale. But given the state of that position group in San Francisco right now, it will be surprising if Stribling isn't out there in Week 1 when San Francisco faces the Rams in Australia.

This isn't a surprise, either. But it's becoming a real concern.

We knew the Niners were thin up front defensively. Nick Bosa is tentatively expected to play Week 1, but he has seen precious little activity this summer as he works his way back from ACL tear. Mykel Williams is trying to return from the same injury, but he's not going to be ready to take on the Rams.

The depth behind that duo isn't especially imposing, and it showed in the preseason. Fortunately for San Francisco, two of the team's first three games are against tomato cans. But if the team can't get the pass rush squared away soon, getting after opposing quarterbacks is going to be a problem.

To be clear, it's not especially likely that Jalen Milroe will open the season as Sam Darnold's backup in the Windy City. That job is Drew Lock's.

But there was some worry that Milroe wouldn't make the team at all after a shaky preseason outing against the Tennessee Titans. The second-year pro responded with a much stronger outing against the Kansas City Chiefs—a showing that head coach Mike Macdonald talked up while addressing the media .

"Thought Jalen Milroe played a really good game," head coach Mike Macdonald said. "Took care of the football and was decisive, made some really strong throws down the field, put us in a position to win there at the end."

There's no question who Seattle's top-two cornerbacks are—the newly-paid Devon Witherspoon and Josh Jobe.

After that though? The questions start adding up—quickly.

The Seahawks signed seventh-year veteran Noah Igbinoghene in free agency. Added three cornerbacks in the draft. Signed former Pro Bowler Trevon Diggs in August. On Sunday they swung a trade with the Los Angeles Chargers for rookie Avery Smith.

But one of those rookies Seattle drafted (Michael Dansby) was let go at final cuts. Both Igbinoghene and Diggs were widely regarded to be on the roster bubble themselves. Smith was a UDFA.

Seattle appears to just be throwing cornerbacks at the wall in the hopes one sticks.

And there's a lot of uncertainty at the back end of the Seahawks defense.

In six years at the University of Kansas, Jalon Daniels became one of two players in Jayhawks history to amass 10,000 yards of offense. He's second in school history in passing yards.

That wasn't enough to get Daniels drafted, but when the 2026 NFL season begins he'll be on an active roster.

Daniels had a solid camp and excellent preseason, completing 27 of 44 passes for 239 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. The Buccaneers saw enough from the youngster to move on from Browning, making Daniels Baker Mayfield's backup in Tampa.

An undrafted rookie out of LSU, Pyburn was always a longshot to make Tampa's 53-man roster. But the 6'4" 258-pounder did his best to make it a difficult decision, backing up a solid training camp by leading the NFL in preseason sacks with four.

That wasn't enough for Pyburn to stick though—he was waived by the Buccaneers on Sunday. The wild part is what could be coming next.

Unless another team claims Pyburn off waivers, he intends to return to LSU to play for Lane Kiffin—he is a plaintiff in one of the lawsuits aimed at forcing retroactive application of the NCAA's new five-year rule.

Restrepo spent most of his rookie season on Tennessee's practice squad, although he was active for two games. But the former Miami standout was consistently one of the hardest-working players on the practice field this summer, and he closed the preseason strong with four catches for 71 yards in the finale.

While speaking to reporters , Restrepo made it clear he won't be satisfied until he's on the 53-man roster.

"Obviously, I'm not satisfied at all with being on the practice squad," he said, "but I think nobody is satisfied with that, right? Because that's why we play football. I think the goal is definitely make plays when it counts."

Restrepo made enough of those plays to get his wish.

The reign of the Mayonnaise kid is over.

As recently as two years ago, Will Levis started 12 games under center for the Titans. The problem is that Levis was wildly erratic in 21 starts over two seasons in Nashville. For every throw that was on target another was airmailed. His decision-making under pressure was terrible, which resulted in turnovers that had to be seen to be believed.

Levis missed the entire 2025 season after undergoing shoulder surgery, and after a shaky camp the team decided there was no room on the roster for Levis behind starter Cam Ward and veteran backup Mitchell Trubisky.

Someone will likely take a flier on the former second-rounder.

After spending the first four years of his career in Washington Settle is back for a second stint with the team after four years with the Houston Texans and Buffalo Bills. It has been a bumpy offseason for the veteran—he had foot surgery and then missed time in camp with a bad calf.

However, Settle was able to get some game reps in during the first half of the final preseason game and looked good. That's good news for the team—not only is Settle expected to start alongside Da'Ron Payne and Javon Kinlaw in Washington's new 3-4 defense, but with Johnny Newton out with a pectoral tear depth on the defensive front is shaky at present.

Trent Scott has been kicking around the NFL for some time—the 32-year-old has spent eight years in the NFL on four different teams. He has played all over the offensive line, making starts at both guard and tackle—26 in all.

Given that experience, versatility and the fact he made three starts for the Commanders last year, it would seem he'd be a good candidate for a reserve spot.

But not only was Scott on the field late in Washington's preseason finale, but he struggled in the game. Neither is a good sign, and Scott was cut by the Commanders on Sunday.

articles.title: Steelers keep both Drew Allar, Will Howard behind Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph at QB
articles.summary: The Steelers also traded OT Broderick Jones and RB Kaleb Johnson in noteworthy moves en route to finalizing the 53-man regular-season roster.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers announced their 53-man roster for the regular season on Sunday, Aug. 30 and made the unorthodox move many expected them to while parting ways with some former top draft picks.

GM Omar Khan and coach Mike McCarthy elected to carry four quarterbacks : Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and Drew Allar. Rodgers will start during the 2026 season before retiring in 2027. Mason Rudolph will play out the one year remaining on his deal as the primary backup. Howard and Allar will develop under an offensive-minded coach known for quarterback development.

The front office also made trades involving former 2023 first-round pick Broderick Jones , an offensive tackle, and 2025 third-round pick Kaleb Johnson , a running back.

Take a look at the home stadiums for all 32 NFL teams

Most NFL teams carry no more than three quarterbacks. Some carry two, with an emergency option stashed on the practice squad.

The Steelers, however, found themselves in a unique position with Rodgers entering his final NFL season. Keeping Rudolph, a battle-tested backup, gives their current roster the best chance to win in the event of a Rodgers injury at some point.

Keeping Allar and Howard sets up a possible competition for the starting job in 2027 with another year of seasoning under their respective belts. Howard is in his second season after leading Ohio State to the 2024 national title. He had three touchdowns and three turnovers during a preseason of mixed results. Allar was a third-round pick in the NFL draft this past spring. He showed more consistency with four total touchdowns and no interceptions but struggled with accuracy and drops from receivers at times.

Of course, Khan and McCarthy could always opt to add to their mix with a veteran or a top NFL draft pick next year. For now, though, these two seem to be their preferred possible answers to the quarterback question that has dogged the team since Ben Roethlisberger retired in 2021.

Steelers trade Broderick Jones and Kaleb Johnson

The Jones trade to the Dallas Cowboys was a bit unexpected because he was their most proven option at the position beyond starters Troy Fautanu and Dylan Cook. Max Iheanachor was the team's top draft pick in April, but he's gotten limited reps in training camp and the preseason. It appears the team is comfortable enough with what it has seen to make him the swing tackle who can push Cook for playing time. The Steelers sent a fourth-round pick with Jones in exchange for third and sixth round picks in 2027

Johnson was only a Steeler for a little over a year after being selected following an outstanding final season at Iowa in which he totaled 1,537 yards and 21 rushing touchdowns. McCarthy deployed him sparingly in two of the preseason games, signaling that he might be in trouble. He'll now join the Green Bay Packers in exchange for a sixth-round pick .

Elandon Roberts and Malik Harrison were among the more notable cuts of the day. Roberts signed a few weeks ago after serving as a key run stuffer for former coach Mike Tomlin's defense from 2023-24. He played for new Steelers DC Patrick Graham last season in Las Vegas.

Harrison signed a two-year deal last season, but played sparingly in the preseason. He was set to make close to $5 million, so this move frees up a significant amount of salary cap space.

In addition to Allar, the Steelers decided to keep all 10 of their draft picks. That includes running back Eli Heidenreich, the Pittsburgh-area native and Navy product whom the team drafted in the seventh round this spring. He beat out veterans Lew Nichols and Travis Homer in addition to Johnson to claim his spot.

On the injury front, Joey Porter Jr. was activated from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. He missed all of training camp and the preseason with a listed back injury, but the team has also acknowledged an impasse in contract negotiations that might have been a factor in his decision to sit out. Starting safety DeShon Elliott was placed on the reserve/injured list and is set to miss the first four games of the season.

articles.title: Pair of former Spartans released by Los Angeles Rams
articles.summary: A pair of former Spartans were released by the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
It is one of the hardest days on the calendar for players in the National Football League, as NFL teams have to cut their roster sizes down to just 53 players, making a lot players in need of finding new homes. A pair of former Spartans were on the wrong side of the news cycle today, failing to make a 53-man roster.

Offensive tackle AJ Arcuri and punter Jack Bouwmeester were cut by the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.

Bouwmeester, a punter at MSU in 2019, has yet to stick anywhere in the NFL. Arcuri, a standout offensive lineman for Michigan State from 2016-2021, was drafted by the Rams in the 7th round of the 2022 NFL Draft. Since then, he has spent his entire career with the organization, appearing in 10 games and making one start.

Now, both former Spartans will be looking for a practice squad home to continue their dreams of playing professional football.

The NFL placed running back Josh Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list to open the 2026 season, creating an additional spot on the roster. While on the exempt list, Jacobs will receive pay but will not be eligible to participate in practices or games. This comes after Jacobs was charged with two misdemeanors, one count of battery and another count of criminal damage to property, stemming from his late May arrest.

articles.title: Denver Broncos have placed TE Caleb Lohner on injured reserve
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos have placed former seventh-round 2025 NFL Draft pick tight end Caleb Lohner on injured reserve.
articles.body:
According to Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post, the Denver Broncos have placed former seventh-round 2025 NFL Draft pick tight end Caleb Lohner on injured reserve.

Lohner was a basketball player who made a late transition to football in college. His measurables are off the charts for tight end, but he'll likely need more development than your typical tight end. He needed to have a standout camp to move the needle . Instead, he spent some time with an injury and that was much-needed time on the practice field missed.

Being a standout player at a rookie minicamp is one thing, but if he can continue to stand out during OTAs and minicamp moving forward, that hype train could be a fun one as we head into training camp.

Being placed on short-term injured reserve should give Denver more time to evaluate Lohner's development. If he ends up not on the 53-man roster, he would certainly be a strong practice squad candidate.
